Hi Emma —

Appreciate the clear list — answering inline below and attaching a concise residency matrix and retention summary for your packet (Residency-Matrix-Apr2029.xlsx, Retention-Summary-Apr2029.pdf). If you want we can turn this into a short slide for procurement.

1) Where request content lives - Hosted API flow: incoming request content is accepted by the Redwood front door in the requested region (we serve from multiple cloud regions). By default, request content is treated as ephemeral:
   - In-flight and model KV caches: held in memory on the serving nodes (GPU/edge), with automatic eviction based on cache policies. TTL for KV/prefix caches is typically seconds to minutes and not written to persistent storage.
   - Short-term request buffers and audit traces: persisted to an encrypted, region-scoped storage tier for operational debugging only. This storage is encrypted at rest with Redwoods' KMS. By default the operational buffer is retained for 7 days; see item 2 for configurable windows.
   - Persistent storage: Redwood does not persist customer request content to long-term object storage for hosted API unless a customer opts into features that require retention (e.g., fine-grained usage analytics, custom evals or embeddings store).

2) Default retention windows and per-tenant controls - Defaults (hosted API):
   - Request payloads: 7 days (operational buffer), automatically purged thereafter unless customer enables extended retention.
   - Model outputs and responses: 7 days.
   - Embeddings: not stored by default. If a customer enables the embeddings store feature, data is retained according to the customer's selected retention policy (default 90 days) and can be configured to 0/30/90/365 days or indefinite under enterprise contract.
   - Audit logs (API metadata, error traces): 90 days by default. Customers on Dedicated/Private can request extended retention windows and exported logs.

   Controls: Customers can select retention profiles during onboarding (self-service in Console) or request custom retention via contract for enterprise plans. For hosted customers: onboarding options are 7/30/90/365 days for payloads & outputs; embeddings are an opt-in store with independent retention settings.

3) Backups / snapshots -
   - Backups of control plane configuration and model artifacts are taken nightly and retained for 30 days by default in the originating region. These backups do not include raw customer request payloads unless the customer has explicitly enabled persistent analytics or data export.
   - For disaster recovery we maintain cross-region backups for control plane metadata (30-day retention) and replicate model binaries to a second region; these copies are encrypted in transit and at rest.

4) Evidence deliverables (attached)
   - Residency-Matrix-Apr2029.xlsx: maps which regions store which classes of data and the fallback region behavior.
   - Retention-Summary-Apr2029.pdf: concise policy, retention windows, configuration options and deletion guarantees.

Additional technical notes and guarantees -
   - Deletion timeline: when a customer requests erasure via Console or API, we perform immediate logical deletion from the active stores and trigger purge jobs for backups/snapshots. Logical deletion completes within 48 hours; residual snapshots (if applicable) are expunged within 30 days (documented in the Retention-Summary).
   - Proof of deletion / attestations: we provide deletion receipts for controlled erasures and can include a time-stamped audit log entry for enterprise contracts.
   - Encryption & keys: hosted API uses provider-managed KMS by default; we offer customer-managed keys (CMK) on enterprise hosted contracts for additional control over at-rest keys.
   - Data residency: for hosted API we pin storage and operational buffers to the customer-selected region(s). Smart routing will pick the nearest region by policy; we include a region-lock option (contract required) to prevent cross-region fallback except for critical failover.

If you want a short whitepaper on deletion timelines and proof artifacts I can have Marissa pull the SOC2 excerpts and the retention policy appendix.

Hi Emma —

Following up with the precise language and attachments for your Ops & security files. See SOC2 extract and the retention paragraph below, and attached full SOC2 Type II report for your compliance team (SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-Apr2029.pdf).

Official deletion timeline (copy/paste for runbook):
"Within 48 hours of a customer-initiated erasure request, Redwood Inference performs logical deletion from active stores and marks the tenant data as deleted. Automated purge jobs then remove residual entries from operational buffers and caches. Any backups or snapshots that include the tenant's data are scheduled for expungement; expungement completes within 30 calendar days from the deletion request, during which time the backup copies remain encrypted and inaccessible via normal administrative interfaces. A deletion receipt (time-stamped) will be generated and can be delivered via the Console or API endpoint specified in the contract."

Responses to your infra questions:
A) Ephemeral copies / snapshots: Backups/snapshots are not considered part of the active store. They are immutable copies created for recovery and are subject to the 30-day expungement window above. While the snapshot exists it remains encrypted and access-controlled; we do not surface snapshot contents to operators without a documented legal or customer-approved process.
B) Embeddings store encryption & BYOK: The embeddings store supports AES-256 at rest. For enterprise hosted customers we support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via Cloud KMS integration (customer-managed keys). When BYOK is enabled, key usage logs are available to the customer subject to contract terms.
C) Region-lock — outage mode: If region-lock is enabled in the customer's contract, Redwood will not automatically fail over to another region for normal traffic. During a region-wide outage the behavior options are:
   - Fail closed (default for strict region-lock): requests will fail with a 5xx indicating regional unavailability.
   - Controlled failover (optional addendum): Redwood can be contracted to failover to a secondary region; any cross-region processing will be logged and an SLA exception is documented.
